```{r packages}
# install.packages(c("dplyr", "tidyr", "readr", "ggplot2", "cluster", "ranger", "pROC", "knitr"))
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(cluster)   # silhouette
library(ranger)    # fast random forest
library(pROC)      # AUC / ROC curves
library(knitr)     # kable tables

set.seed(707)
```

# Overview

This analysis uses NFL Combine results merged with draft and career data (from `02_merge_data.R`) to answer two questions:

1. **Are there distinct athletic archetypes among Combine participants, and do they differ in career outcomes?** (unsupervised — k-means clustering)
2. **Can Combine results predict which players become multi-year NFL starters?** (supervised — logistic regression and random forest)

# Data Preparation

```{r load}
nfl <- read_csv("nfl_combine_career_data.csv", na = c("NA", ""), show_col_types = FALSE)
dim(nfl)
```

## Cleaning decisions

- **Height** is stored as text ("6-4") and is converted to inches.
- **Positions** are collapsed from ~25 labels into 9 groups. Kickers, punters, and long snappers are dropped because Combine drills are not relevant to them.
- **Only 2000–2019 draft classes** are kept. Players from 2020 onward have not had enough seasons for "success" to be known.
- **Undrafted players** do not appear in the draft table, so their career stats are set to 0. This is a limitation: some undrafted free agents did have NFL careers.

```{r clean}
ht_to_in <- function(h) {
  parts <- strsplit(as.character(h), "-")
  sapply(parts, function(p) if (length(p) == 2) as.numeric(p[1]) * 12 + as.numeric(p[2]) else NA_real_)
}

pos_groups <- c(
  QB = "QB", RB = "RB", FB = "RB", WR = "WR", TE = "TE",
  OT = "OL", OG = "OL", G = "OL", C = "OL", OL = "OL",
  DT = "DL", DL = "DL", DE = "EDGE", EDGE = "EDGE",
  OLB = "LB", ILB = "LB", LB = "LB",
  CB = "DB", S = "DB", SAF = "DB", DB = "DB"
)

drills <- c("ht_in", "wt", "forty", "bench", "vertical", "broad_jump", "cone", "shuttle")

nfl_clean <- nfl %>%
  mutate(
    ht_in     = ht_to_in(ht),
    across(c(wt, forty, bench, vertical, broad_jump, cone, shuttle,
             round, pick, w_av, games, seasons_started, probowls), as.numeric),
    pos_group = unname(pos_groups[pos])
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(pos_group)) %>%
  filter(season.x >= 2000, season.x <= 2019) %>%
  mutate(
    drafted = as.integer(!is.na(round)),
    across(c(w_av, games, seasons_started, probowls), ~ replace_na(.x, 0)),
    success = factor(ifelse(seasons_started >= 3, "yes", "no"), levels = c("no", "yes"))
  )

nrow(nfl_clean)
```

## Defining success

The target variable is **success = became a starter for 3 or more seasons**.

```{r target}
nfl_clean %>%
  count(success) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1)) %>%
  kable(caption = "Overall success rate")

nfl_clean %>%
  group_by(pos_group) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), pct_starter = round(mean(success == "yes") * 100, 1)) %>%
  arrange(desc(pct_starter)) %>%
  kable(caption = "Success rate by position group")
```

## Position-adjusted drill scores

A 4.6-second 40-yard dash is elite for a defensive tackle and slow for a cornerback. To compare players fairly, every drill is converted to a **z-score within the player's position group**.

```{r zscores}
nfl_clean <- nfl_clean %>%
  group_by(pos_group) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(drills),
                ~ (.x - mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                .names = "{.col}_z")) %>%
  ungroup()
```

## Missing drill results

Many players skip some drills, so missingness is substantial for bench, cone, and shuttle.

```{r missing}
nfl_clean %>%
  summarise(across(all_of(drills), ~ round(mean(is.na(.x)) * 100, 1))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "drill", values_to = "pct_missing") %>%
  kable(caption = "Percent missing by drill")
```

Each missing value is flagged with an indicator (skipping a drill can itself be a signal), then filled with z = 0, the average for that player's position. Timed drills are sign-flipped so that **higher always means better** in the cluster profiles.

```{r impute}
z_cols <- paste0(drills, "_z")

nfl_clean <- nfl_clean %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(drills), ~ as.integer(is.na(.x)), .names = "{.col}_miss")) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(z_cols), ~ replace_na(.x, 0))) %>%
  mutate(speed_z    = -forty_z,
         cone_zr    = -cone_z,
         shuttle_zr = -shuttle_z)
```

# Clustering: Athletic Archetypes

K-means clustering groups players by their position-adjusted athletic profile.

```{r clust-data}
clust_vars <- c("speed_z", "vertical_z", "broad_jump_z", "bench_z",
                "wt_z", "cone_zr", "shuttle_zr")
clust_data <- nfl_clean %>% select(all_of(clust_vars))
```

## Choosing the number of clusters

```{r choose-k}
k_range <- 2:8
wss <- sapply(k_range, function(k) kmeans(clust_data, k, nstart = 25)$tot.withinss)

sil_sample <- sample(nrow(clust_data), 3000)
d_sample   <- dist(clust_data[sil_sample, ])
sil <- sapply(k_range, function(k) {
  km <- kmeans(clust_data, k, nstart = 25)
  mean(silhouette(km$cluster[sil_sample], d_sample)[, 3])
})

k_eval <- data.frame(k = k_range, wss = round(wss), silhouette = round(sil, 3))
kable(k_eval, caption = "Elbow and silhouette by k")

ggplot(k_eval, aes(k, wss)) + geom_line() + geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Elbow plot", y = "Total within-cluster sum of squares") +
  theme_minimal()
```

k = 4 gave the best silhouette in testing (about 0.15). A low silhouette is expected here: athleticism is a continuum rather than a set of sharply separated groups, so the clusters are best read as **interpretable profiles**.

## Cluster profiles

```{r kmeans}
km <- kmeans(clust_data, centers = 4, nstart = 50)
nfl_clean$cluster <- factor(km$cluster)

cluster_profile <- nfl_clean %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  summarise(
    n            = n(),
    speed        = mean(speed_z),
    vertical     = mean(vertical_z),
    broad        = mean(broad_jump_z),
    bench        = mean(bench_z),
    weight       = mean(wt_z),
    pct_drafted  = mean(drafted) * 100,
    avg_pick     = mean(pick, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_starter  = mean(success == "yes") * 100,
    avg_w_av     = mean(w_av),
    pct_probowl  = mean(probowls > 0) * 100
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2)))

kable(cluster_profile, caption = "Athletic profile and career outcomes by cluster")
```

**Interpretation.** Cluster numbers change between runs, so match clusters by their profile. In testing they came out roughly as:

| Archetype | Profile | Starter rate |
|---|---|---|
| Explosive athletes | Fast, big jumps | ~40% |
| Big & strong | Heavy for position, strong bench | ~32% |
| Undersized / average | Light, slightly below average | ~27% |
| Below-average movers | Slow, poor jumps | ~18% |

## Is cluster related to success?

```{r chisq}
chisq.test(table(nfl_clean$cluster, nfl_clean$success))
```

## Visualizing the clusters

```{r pca}
pca <- prcomp(clust_data)
summary(pca)$importance[, 1:3]

pca_df <- data.frame(pca$x[, 1:2], cluster = nfl_clean$cluster)
ggplot(pca_df, aes(PC1, PC2, color = cluster)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "Athletic archetypes (k-means, PCA projection)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r cluster-by-pos, fig.height=5.5}
nfl_clean %>%
  group_by(pos_group, cluster) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), pct_starter = mean(success == "yes") * 100, .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(pos_group, pct_starter, fill = cluster)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(title = "Starter rate by athletic archetype and position",
       y = "% who became 3+ year starters", x = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Supervised Models: Predicting Multi-Year Starters

## Train/test split

The models train on **2000–2015** draft classes and are tested on **2016–2019**. This time-based split mimics real use (predicting a new class from past ones) and avoids leakage between years.

Two feature sets are compared:

- **Combine only**: position-adjusted drill z-scores, missing-drill flags, position group
- **Combine + draft pick**: adds where the player was drafted (undrafted = pick 300), measuring how much NFL teams already know beyond the Combine

```{r split}
miss_cols <- paste0(drills, "_miss")
combine_feats <- c(z_cols, miss_cols, "pos_group")

model_df <- nfl_clean %>%
  mutate(pos_group = factor(pos_group),
         pick_filled = ifelse(is.na(pick), 300, pick))

train <- model_df %>% filter(season.x <= 2015)
test  <- model_df %>% filter(season.x >= 2016)

c(train = nrow(train), test = nrow(test))

f_combine <- as.formula(paste("success ~", paste(combine_feats, collapse = " + ")))
f_full    <- update(f_combine, . ~ . + pick_filled)

auc_of <- function(probs) as.numeric(auc(roc(test$success, probs, quiet = TRUE)))
```

## Model fitting

```{r models}
# Logistic regression
logit_A <- glm(f_combine, data = train, family = binomial)
logit_B <- glm(f_full,    data = train, family = binomial)
p_logit_A <- predict(logit_A, test, type = "response")
p_logit_B <- predict(logit_B, test, type = "response")

# Random forest
rf_A <- ranger(f_combine, data = train, num.trees = 500, min.node.size = 10,
               probability = TRUE, importance = "permutation")
rf_B <- ranger(f_full, data = train, num.trees = 500, min.node.size = 10,
               probability = TRUE, importance = "permutation")
p_rf_A <- predict(rf_A, test)$predictions[, "yes"]
p_rf_B <- predict(rf_B, test)$predictions[, "yes"]
```

## Results

```{r results}
results <- data.frame(
  model = c("Logistic — combine only", "Random forest — combine only",
            "Logistic — combine + pick", "Random forest — combine + pick"),
  test_AUC = round(c(auc_of(p_logit_A), auc_of(p_rf_A),
                     auc_of(p_logit_B), auc_of(p_rf_B)), 3)
)
kable(results, caption = "Test-set AUC (2016–2019 classes)")
```

In the prototype, combine-only models reached an AUC of about **0.69** and adding draft pick raised it to about **0.88**. The Combine carries real but modest signal; most of what predicts a career is already reflected in where teams draft a player.

```{r roc}
plot(roc(test$success, p_rf_A, quiet = TRUE), col = "steelblue",
     main = "ROC: who becomes a 3+ year starter")
plot(roc(test$success, p_rf_B, quiet = TRUE), col = "darkred", add = TRUE)
legend("bottomright", c("Combine only", "Combine + draft pick"),
       col = c("steelblue", "darkred"), lwd = 2)
```

## Confusion matrix

Because only about 29% of players become multi-year starters, a cutoff of 0.3 is used instead of 0.5.

```{r confusion}
cutoff <- 0.3
cm <- table(predicted = ifelse(p_rf_A > cutoff, "yes", "no"), actual = test$success)
cm
cat("Accuracy:", round(sum(diag(cm)) / sum(cm), 3), "\n")
```

## Logistic regression coefficients

```{r logit-coef}
coef_tbl <- summary(logit_A)$coefficients
kable(round(coef_tbl[order(coef_tbl[, 4]), ][1:12, ], 4),
      caption = "Most significant predictors (combine-only logistic model)")
```

## Feature importance

```{r importance}
imp <- sort(rf_A$variable.importance, decreasing = TRUE)
data.frame(feature = names(imp), importance = imp) %>%
  head(12) %>%
  ggplot(aes(reorder(feature, importance), importance)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") + coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Random forest feature importance (combine only)", x = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

In testing, position-adjusted 40-yard dash and weight were the strongest signals.

# Extension: Predicting Career Value

As a continuous outcome, a random forest predicts weighted career Approximate Value (`w_av`) for drafted players only.

```{r wav}
drafted_train <- train %>% filter(drafted == 1)
drafted_test  <- test  %>% filter(drafted == 1)

f_wav <- as.formula(paste("w_av ~", paste(combine_feats, collapse = " + ")))
rf_wav <- ranger(f_wav, data = drafted_train, num.trees = 500, min.node.size = 10)
pred_wav <- predict(rf_wav, drafted_test)$predictions

data.frame(
  RMSE = round(sqrt(mean((pred_wav - drafted_test$w_av)^2)), 2),
  R2   = round(cor(pred_wav, drafted_test$w_av)^2, 3)
) %>% kable(caption = "Career value regression (test set)")
```

Note: 2016–2019 players are still accumulating career value, so this R² understates the model's true skill.

# Conclusions

- **Athletic archetypes exist and relate to outcomes.** Explosive players became multi-year starters at roughly twice the rate of slow, poor-jumping players.
- **Combine results alone predict career success modestly** (AUC ≈ 0.69).
- **Draft position adds far more** (AUC ≈ 0.88), suggesting teams already incorporate most Combine information plus film and scouting that the Combine does not capture.

## Limitations

- Undrafted players are assigned zero career value, which undercounts successful undrafted free agents.
- Drill missingness is high for bench, cone, and shuttle; mean imputation within position may blur differences.
- "3+ seasons as a starter" is one definition of success; results could differ for Pro Bowls or career length.
